title: Why are young men staying single? Study blames social media, affordability | Institute for Family Studies
gist: NewsNation brief on an IFS study: about 70% of US men under 25 are single and half of those are not looking for a girlfriend, a sharp shift from 2019; guests attribute the trend to social media and affordability.

themes.theme: Young men opting out of dating

insights.claim: About 70% of US men under 25 are single, per an Institute for Family Studies study.
insights.speaker: Katie Pavlich (News Nation)
insights.so_what: Signals delayed household formation and weaker demand for couple/family-oriented goods.
insights.quote: about 70% of men under 25 are single

insights.claim: Half of single young men are not looking for a girlfriend, a sharp shift from 2019 when most said they wanted one, according to Gen Z journalist Eli Thompson.
insights.speaker: Eli Thompson
insights.so_what: Rapid preference shift toward voluntary singlehood among Gen Z men.
insights.quote: Half of them aren’t even looking for a girlfriend

insights.claim: Guests on 'Katie Pavlich Tonight' attribute rising voluntary singlehood among young men to social media and affordability pressures, reshaping Gen Z dating and marriage.
insights.speaker: Katie Pavlich (News Nation)
insights.so_what: Affordability as a driver links housing/cost of living to family formation.
